pr_comments: @cdce8p or @epenet does either of you have time for a review? Basically I'm trying to implement a fix for an issue which currently prevents the wallbox integration from working. Root cause of this issue is a JWT token of the api that expires (earlier than expected). The fix I'm implementing here is forcing the token to be empty so it is always being refreshed. I consider this a temp fix;  everybody is now suffering from this issue and this solution works. However, I'm trying to find a more elegant solution in which the token is refreshed less often.
@balloob small bump, I really like this PR to be merged to fix the issue. I think that the change now is quite minor (but the issue quite significant)
@cdce8p or @epenet maybe one of you has time for a review? Hate to be pushy, but this is a fix for an issue which currently blocks the use of the wallbox integration.

All, so I'm trying to get a very basic fix merged. Problem we are facing is that the Wallbox API token expires too early, causing the connection/security error. I'm now trying to merge a temp solution in which we update the token on every data update (by clearing it first, forcing an update). This works, but is not very nice, however, I haven't been able to find a better, more reliable solution this weekend... So, temp solution for now. Hopefully something better later.

`    def _authenticate(self) -> None:
        """Authenticate using Wallbox API."""
        try:
            # Force authentication if the token is about to expire, necessary due to timegap between authenticate and get_data:
            self._wallbox.jwtToken = ""
            self._wallbox.authenticate()`

This is the fix, you van change this method in the init package of the wallbox integration if you want.

If you are stuck reloding the intagration using nodered from time to time (or when you need it) might be a temp fix.
See: https://community.home-assistant.io/t/node-red-flow-to-reload-an-integration/267674/5

into

if self.jwtToken != "" and (self.jwtTokenTtl/1000) > datetime.timestamp(datetime.now()):

At tis time, it is solved by having an automation reload Walbox every 12 minutes. This resets the timestamp and you're ok for 15 minutes:

alias: Reload Walbox application every 12 minutes
description: ""
trigger:
  - platform: time_pattern
    minutes: /12
condition: []
action:
  - service: homeassistant.reload_config_entry
    data: {}
    target:
      device_id: aa5ab194573f6b93c6a7e3fd0ddc6d72 (= my Wallbox integration)
mode: single

This change in wallbox.py seems to fix the connection drop every 15min, basic idea is to renew the token before it expires.

`if self.jwtToken != "" and (self.jwtTokenTtl/1000) > (datetime.timestamp(datetime.now())+120)`

if self.jwtToken != "" and (self.jwtTokenTtl/1000) > (datetime.timestamp(datetime.now()) -> the division by thousand fixes the underlying issue we had (which was that the wallbox team decided to use miliseconds all of the sudden). I did a version bump in hass (to the new wallbox package with the new fix). 2022.10.4 contains this version bump, it also catches the error better.

The improved error catching allows for the re-connect after an update failure (thus, 1 refresh missed, 30seconds lost). I think we still have an occassional error due to the fact that the wallbox PyPi package doesn't use margins in determining whether the token has expired. The idea of @christerrex might indeed be the solution. I'm running a debug version of the integration to see if this indeed is the reason of the short drops in connection.
However, if this is the problem and fix, please note that this is not a Home Assistant issue. This is an issue in wallbox PyPi package.
